passages.passage_text: In the underworld drug cartel of Sinaloa (Mexico), Cristobal a former student of chemistry started cooking a drug known as methamphetamine. For the first time in the year 1893, in Japan this powerful drug was derived from ephedrine an alkaloid found in ephedra plant. Initially used as medicine and during war time to keep soldiers awake, it's misuse turned it into one of the most destructive drugs of abuse globally. His cartel used to smuggle the drug concealed in different consignments all over the world. Methamphetamine gained popularity in a short span and was preferred over the traditional ones as it floods the brain with dopamine, creating extreme euphoria but on the other hand, leads to severe addiction, paranoia, neurological damage etc. As Cristobal seals a shipment, he knows, he is creating a fortune and at the same time wiping out the young generation. Born from a desert shrub, transformed by chemist and trafficked across continents-methamphetamine is a global curse wrapped in glittering crystals.

In a case of murder, the victim was killed with a semi-automatic pistol. The said killing was well planned. The injured victim was shifted to the nearest hospital where he succumbed to his injuries the next day. Meantime, the suspect/accused visited the said scene and picked up the cartridge case left while firing and vanished from the scene of the crime. The police searched the scene of occurrence next morning for the cartridge, but found none.
The suspect/accused was caught by the police after few days and a weapon was recovered from him. Police placed one fired cartridge and showed the recovery of the cartridge from the scene on the next day of the crime. However, they made two mistakes:
1. The cartridge case was shown at a distance of about 12 feet. The forensic surgeon and ballistic expert reported it as a close range shot.
2. The jacket part recovered from the dead body did not form part of the cartridge of which the cartridge case was found at the scene formed part. The manufacturer had not manufactured any cartridge which had jacket covering the bullet base corresponding to the one recovered from the body of the victim.
The experts did not find any evidence to link or delink the jacket with the pistol recovered from the suspect/accused.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are correct regarding fingerprint identification?

statements.label: A
statements.text: Level 1 details include the general ridge flow and pattern configuration.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Level 1 details are sufficient for individualization.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Level 2 details, that is, ridge endings, bifurcations etc. are used for exclusion.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Level 2 details such as dots, bifurcation, combination thereof etc. are used for individualization.

questions.explanation: Fingerprint identification involves three levels of detail. Level 1 provides the general ridge flow and pattern types such as loops, whorls, and arches. These are useful for classifying fingerprints but not sufficient for proving identity. For personal identification, forensic experts rely on Level 2 details, which include ridge endings, bifurcations, dots, and combinations of these minutiae. These finer characteristics are unique to every individual and serve as the basis for personal identification. Thus, Level 1 is only for classification, while Level 2 is the true source of uniqueness.

questions.question_text: Arrange in proper sequence the steps followed in any forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) during submission of biological exhibits for examination:

statements.label: A
statements.text: If the case falls under concerned FSL jurisdiction

statements.label: B
statements.text: Checking of proper sealing of exhibits and if sample of seal is provided

questions.explanation: In the submission of biological exhibits to an FSL, the process is methodical to ensure security and authenticity. The first step is checking whether the case falls under the jurisdiction of the concerned laboratory (A). Next, the submission letter or authorization from the investigating authority is verified (D). After authorization, the exhibits are examined for proper sealing and the presence of a sample seal to confirm integrity (B). Finally, after these formalities, the exhibits are photographed for record and documentation (C).

questions.question_text: The greenish discoloration in early putrefaction is normally caused due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: The greenish discoloration of the lower abdomen seen in the early stage of putrefaction is due to sulphmethaemoglobin. When decomposition begins, bacteria release hydrogen sulphide, which reacts with haemoglobin in the blood to form this greenish pigment. This color change is one of the earliest external signs of putrefaction and helps forensic experts estimate the post-mortem interval.

questions.question_text: Which of the undermentioned poisonous plants belong to family Solanaceae?
questions.explanation: The Solanaceae family, or nightshade family, includes several poisonous plants. Atropa (deadly nightshade) contains atropine, Hyoscyamus (henbane) contains hyoscyamine and scopolamine, and Nicotina (tobacco) produces nicotine. These belong to Solanaceae and are medically significant due to their alkaloids. Digitalis, however, belongs to Scrophulariaceae, and Lamium belongs to Lamiaceae, so they are not included. Hence, Atropa, Hyoscyamus, and Nicotina are the correct members.

questions.question_text: From the examples given below select the name of anabolic steroids:
questions.explanation: Anabolic steroids are artificial substances derived from testosterone and used to promote muscle growth. Oxandrolene is a steroid used in weight gain treatments, Stanozolol is a synthetic anabolic steroid commonly misused by athletes, and Nandrolene is another anabolic steroid enhancing protein synthesis. On the other hand, Dilaudid is an opioid painkiller, while Freon is an industrial refrigerant, not related to steroids. Thus, the true anabolic steroids in the list are Oxandrolene, Stanozolol, and Nandrolene.

questions.question_text: During the light interaction with matter, which of the following statements are correct:

statements.label: A
statements.text: The energy of the photon is inversely proportional to the wavelength.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The energy of the photon is directly proportional to the wavelength.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The shorter the wavelength, the higher is the energy of the corresponding photon.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The shorter the wavelength, the lower is the energy of the corresponding photon.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The longer the wavelength, the lower is the energy of the corresponding photon.

questions.explanation: Photon energy E is E = hc/λ. Hence it is inversely proportional to wavelength (A). A shorter wavelength therefore means higher photon energy (C), while a longer wavelength means lower energy (E). Statements B and D contradict this fundamental relation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following techniques are used for separation in analytical chemistry?
questions.explanation: "Separation" methods physically resolve components of a mixture: simple distillation (B) separates by volatility; paper chromatography (C) separates by differential partition; capillary electrophoresis (E) separates by charge-to-size in an electric field. Visible spectrophotometer (A) and polarography (D) are detection/measurement techniques, not primary separation tools.

questions.question_text: Name the gases of decomposition emitted from the dead body during the process of putrefaction.
questions.explanation: Characteristic putrefaction gases from a cadaver include methane (A) and hydrogen sulphide (C)—the latter gives the classic foul odour. Carbon dioxide can be present, but among the given pairings, methane plus hydrogen sulphide best represents gases specifically associated with decomposition odour profiles.

questions.question_text: Arrange in proper sequence:

statements.label: A
statements.text: The rise in temperature causes a sequence of pre-ignition reactions.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The reactions lead to self-sustaining combustion of material.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Explosive material ignited by external stimulus.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The reactions result in transitions in crystalline structures, liquid decomposition and thermal decomposition.

questions.explanation: Sequence of ignition phenomena: an external stimulus ignites the explosive material (C) -> temperature rise triggers pre-ignition reactions (A) -> these reactions drive phase/crystal transitions and thermal decomposition (D) -> the reaction front becomes self-sustaining, leading to combustion (B).

questions.question_text: What is the motto of BPR & D?

options.option_text: Let noble thought come to us from every side

questions.explanation: BPR&D's stated motto is the Rigvedic line "आ नो भद्रा: क्रतवो यन्त्व विश्वतो" rendered in English as "Let noble thoughts come to us from every side", used across its institutions and events to express an open, collaborative research ethos (e.g., BPR&D/PIB communications).

questions.question_text: In doubtful cases, the true sex of an individual can be determined from:
questions.explanation: Sex determination in doubtful cases relies on chromosomal and nuclear evidence: studying sex chromosomes (karyotyping/XX vs. XY) and nuclear sexing (sex chromatin—Barr body/X-chromatin in females; Y-chromatin/F-body tests) provide objective, laboratory-based confirmation. Sibling profiles and outward phenotyping are indirect and may be misleading.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in descending order with respect to complete root calcification (approximately):
questions.explanation: Root calcification completes latest for the third molar (C, ~18–25 yrs), then canines (E, ~13–15 yrs), followed by first bicuspid/premolar (D, ~12–13 yrs), lateral incisor (B, ~10–11 yrs), and earliest for the first molar (A, ~9–10 yrs). Hence the descending order is C -> E -> D -> B -> A.

questions.question_text: With respect to tools used, identifiable tool marks are not found on:
questions.explanation: Identifiable toolmarks require a substrate that can retain microscopic striations or impressions. Liquids like mercury (C) cannot preserve marks, and flexible hoses (E) typically recover elastically, losing fine individual characteristics. In contrast, wood, sealing wax, and metal sheets can retain reproducible tool impressions/striations.

questions.question_text: In micro spectrometers, which type of detector is commonly used?
questions.explanation: Micro-spectrometers in forensic trace work (e.g., micro-FTIR) commonly use MCT detectors for high sensitivity and fast response at microscopic apertures. DTGS and other detectors are used on benches, but MCT is preferred for micro-scale measurements.

questions.question_text: Melancholia is a form of insanity, primarily characterized by:

options.option_text: Mental depression and inhibition of motor impulse

questions.explanation: Melancholia denotes a severe depressive state with pervasive low mood, pessimism, psychomotor retardation (inhibited movement/speech), sleep and appetite changes, and possible guilt or suicidal ideation—distinct from aggression, euphoria, or primary memory disorientation.

questions.question_text: The term "Blue Heaven" is synonym for which of the following?
questions.explanation: The term "Blue Heaven" is sometimes used colloquially for barbiturates like amobarbital, but in toxicological and forensic contexts, it can also be linked with isopropanol. Isopropanol (isopropyl alcohol) is widely used as rubbing alcohol, a solvent, and cleaning agent, and can act as a toxic adulterant in illicit liquors. Its misuse or accidental ingestion is a known cause of poisoning cases, hence the synonym connection in such contexts.

questions.question_text: Central Forensic Science Laboratories are accredited by which of the following agency?

options.option_text: National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories

questions.explanation: Central Forensic Science Laboratories (CFSLs) are accredited by NABL under ISO/IEC 17025 standards. This ensures quality management, technical competence, and international recognition of their forensic testing and calibration services, thereby enhancing the credibility of forensic evidence in courts of law.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are correct statements regarding hair?

statements.label: A
statements.text: The protein of medulla is distinct from the proteins of cortex and cuticle.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Medulla is not present in all human hairs.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The diameter of medulla is largest in the hair of the child, and smallest in old age.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Medulla appears as a network of cellular connections without any spaces or gaps.

questions.explanation: Hair has three main parts: cuticle, cortex, and medulla. The medulla's protein structure differs from the keratin of cortex and cuticle, giving it unique forensic value (A). The medulla is not always present in human hairs—it may be continuous, fragmented, or entirely absent (B). The claim that medulla diameter is largest in children and smallest in the elderly (C) is unsupported, and medulla usually has gaps or air-filled spaces rather than a solid, gap-free structure (D).

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:

match_right.label: I
match_right.text: Strangulation effected by compressing victim's neck against the forearm

match_right.label: III
match_right.text: Victim attacked from back without warning, and strangled by throwing a ligature over the neck and tightening it

match_right.label: IV
match_right.text: Death due to accidental airway obstruction by food

questions.explanation: Garrotting (A-III): A sudden attack from behind with a ligature thrown around the neck and tightened. Cafe Coronary (B-IV): Sudden death caused by food obstructing the airway, often mistaken for a heart attack. Gagging (C-II): Forcibly blocking the mouth, usually with cloth, leading to asphyxia. Mugging (D-I): Strangulation by compressing the neck against the attacker's forearm, a type of chokehold.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II with respect to spermatozoa:
questions.explanation: Head (A-III): Contains the nucleus, essential for fertilization. Middle piece (B-IV): Packed with mitochondria that provide energy. Tail (C-I): Responsible for motility, propelling the sperm. Acrosomal cap (D-II): Stores hydrolytic enzymes that help penetrate the ovum.

questions.question_text: Arrange the process of steam distillation for isolating concentrated accelerants from fire debris:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Volatile hydrocarbons are collected in a liquid form

statements.label: C
statements.text: Heating and distilling with steam of charred material

statements.label: D
statements.text: Trapping the distillate with cold water condenser

questions.explanation: In steam distillation of fire debris, the process begins by heating and distilling the charred material with steam (C). The vapors are condensed and trapped with a cold-water condenser (D). The condensed vapors contain volatile hydrocarbons, which are collected in a liquid form (A). Finally, the collected distillate undergoes chemical analysis to detect accelerants (B).

questions.question_text: The Christiansen's effect is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Christiansen's effect is an optical phenomenon where a suspension becomes transparent at a particular wavelength because the refractive index of the dispersed particles matches that of the medium. Thus, it is directly related to refraction rather than scattering, absorption, or interference.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following explosives in terms of their decreasing performance:
questions.explanation: The performance of explosives is generally ranked by their detonation velocity and brisance. HMX (A) has the highest performance, followed by RDX (B), then PETN (C), and lastly TNT (D), which is the lowest among these four. So the decreasing order is HMX -> RDX -> PETN -> TNT.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: Carbon ink (A-III): Also known as Indian ink, made from fine carbon particles. Iron gallotannate ink (B-IV): Prepared from tannic acid and iron salts. Ball-point pen ink (C-II): Contains dyes dissolved in organic chemical solvents. Porous tip/fiber tip ink (D-I): Fluid, water-based inks used in markers and sketch pens.

questions.question_text: The term in which caseless ammunition gets discharge accidentally due to heat instead of the action of firing pin is known as:
questions.explanation: Cook-offs refer to the accidental discharge of caseless or conventional ammunition due to exposure to high external heat rather than the mechanical action of a firing pin. This is distinct from misfire (failure to fire), backfire (explosion in the wrong direction), or overload (excessive pressure).

questions.question_text: Bite marks collected at the scene of occurrence on humans, involved in sexual crimes can be tested for ptyalin due to the presence of:
questions.explanation: Ptyalin is the salivary amylase enzyme present in human saliva. When bite marks are found on victims in sexual crimes, they may contain traces of saliva deposited by the offender. Testing for ptyalin thus helps confirm the presence of saliva, which can later be used for DNA analysis and individualization.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in proper sequence for Harrison and Gilroy's test:

statements.label: A
statements.text: The test cloth is dried again, a drop of dilute HCl (1:20) is placed over the spot. If the colour changes to blue, lead is indicated. If the colour does not change, barium is indicated.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The gunshot residues are collected on cotton cloth moistened with dilute 0.1 molar HCl.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The dried cloth is treated with two drops of sodium rhodizonate solution (5%). Red colour inside the ring indicates both lead and barium.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The dried cloth piece is treated with one drop of triphenylmethylarsonium iodide alcoholic solution (10%). The appearance of orange ring indicates the presence of antimony.

questions.explanation: The correct sequence of Harrison and Gilroy's test is: first, collect gunshot residues using cotton cloth moistened with dilute HCl (B). Then treat the dried cloth with triphenylmethylarsonium iodide solution, giving an orange ring for antimony (D). Next, add sodium rhodizonate solution to detect both lead and barium by red coloration (C). Finally, apply dilute HCl over the spot—if the colour turns blue, lead is indicated; if no change, barium is confirmed (A).

questions.question_text: From the given compounds which one of the following is commonly used as an adsorbent in thin layer chromatography?
questions.explanation: Sephadex is a cross-linked dextran gel used primarily for gel-filtration column chromatography (size-exclusion), not as a commonly used TLC adsorbent. In TLC, widely used adsorbents are silica gel (e.g., Silica gel G), alumina, cellulose, and calcium carbonate ('G' indicating a gypsum binder). Acrylamide (Option 4) is for electrophoresis gels, and calcium disilicate (Option 2) isn't a standard TLC adsorbent.

questions.question_text: An approximate age of a bruise may be determined from:
questions.explanation: The approximate age of a bruise is estimated by observing the sequential colour changes due to breakdown of haemoglobin (B)—from reddish-blue to bluish-black, green, and yellow. Histological examination (D) under a microscope can further help estimate age by cellular changes. Force applied and vascularity influence bruise formation but not precise age determination.

questions.question_text: Diatoms are present in blood circulation of dead body because diatoms perforate in:
questions.explanation: Diatoms enter the bloodstream during drowning because they pass through ruptured alveolar capillaries in the lungs. From there, they circulate in the bloodstream and may be detected in distant organs and even bone marrow, confirming ante-mortem drowning.

questions.question_text: Any document completely written and signed by one person, is known as:
questions.explanation: A holograph (holographic document) is entirely written and signed by the same person. It's distinct from a hologram (optical image) and an exemplar (specimen writing collected for comparison).

questions.question_text: Arrange the following steps in correct order for performing a competitive solid phase radioimmunoassay to measure cytokine level:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Coat the RIA plate with anti cytokine antibody.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Add a constant amount of 125I labeled cytokine to all wells.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Add increasing concentration of unlabeled cytokine to generate a standard curve.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Add experimental samples to separate wells.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Measure radioactivity and determine cytokine concentrations by comparing with the standard curve.

questions.explanation: Competitive solid-phase RIA workflow: coat plate with anti-cytokine antibody (A) -> add a constant amount of radio-labeled cytokine (B) -> add increasing unlabeled cytokine to build the standard curve (C) -> add unknown samples to separate wells (D) -> measure bound radioactivity and read concentrations from the standard curve (E).

questions.question_text: Rigor mortis sets up due to chemical changes involving ........... and indicates the molecular death of its cells.

options.option_text: Structural proteins of the muscle fibers

questions.explanation: Rigor mortis follows post-mortem ATP depletion, locking actin and myosin (muscle structural proteins) into stable actomyosin cross-bridges. Calcium contributes to contraction, but the hallmark rigidity stems from protein complex fixation when ATP is unavailable.

questions.question_text: Evidence is information provided through:
questions.explanation: Legally recognized evidence is conveyed through witness testimony (B) and documentary/real records (C). Hearsay (D) is generally inadmissible except for limited exceptions, and "AI" (A) is not itself a recognized evidentiary mode.

questions.question_text: In a case of death due to suspected poisoning by carbon monoxide, which sample should be preserved without adding any preservative?
questions.explanation: For suspected carbon monoxide poisoning, blood—kept airtight and filled to the brim—is preserved without additives to accurately quantify carboxyhaemoglobin. Preservatives are unnecessary here and other tissues are less reliable for COHb estimation.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: Fibres are classified based on their origin in plants. Cotton is a seed fibre, produced from the seed hairs of Gossypium, and is one of the world's most important textile fibres (III). Coir is a fruit fibre, obtained from the fibrous mesocarp (husk) of coconut fruit, mainly used for mats, ropes, and brushes (I). Flax is a stem or bast fibre, taken from the inner bark of the flax plant's stem, used to make linen (IV). Manila hemp or abacá is a leaf fibre, derived from the leaf sheaths of Musa textilis (a banana species), prized for making ropes and speciality papers (II).

questions.question_text: In low voltage electrophoresis, which of the following characteristics are normally observed?
questions.explanation: In electrophoresis, the applied voltage controls migration speed and heat generation. At low voltage, the weaker electric field slows molecular migration, producing a longer run time (A). Because heat generated is proportional to the square of voltage, lower voltage causes low heat generation (D), protecting sensitive samples like proteins or nucleic acids. Low voltage does not increase degeneration; in fact, it reduces thermal depends mainly on gel pore size and buffer systems, not simply low voltage.

questions.question_text: The time of ossification from bones gives a good indication of age but few points are to be remembered before giving an opinion, like:

statements.label: B
statements.text: Union of epiphysis in cartilaginous bones

questions.explanation: Using ossification to estimate age requires careful consideration of biological and environmental factors. Nutritional variation (A), such as calcium or vitamin D deficiency, can delay ossification, while good diet can accelerate it. Epiphyseal union in cartilaginous bones (B) occurs at predictable ages, and its presence or absence is a key forensic marker in adolescents and young adults. The statement that tropical conditions are "not considered" is wrong—climatic and genetic factors are always considered. Genotyping (D) helps with personal identification but is unrelated to ossification timing.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of paper-making process:

statements.label: D
statements.text: Refining and sending on Fourdrinier wire

questions.explanation: The paper-making process is stepwise: first, cooking and blowing under pressure (C) treats raw material (like wood chips) with chemicals to break down lignin and release cellulose fibres, producing pulp. Then comes bleaching and beating (A), where fibres are whitened and mechanically beaten to improve bonding. Next, refining and sending on Fourdrinier wire (D) forms a continuous wet sheet as the pulp slurry is spread on a moving mesh. Finally, drying and calendaring (B) removes moisture and passes the sheet through rollers, giving smoothness, gloss, and the required thickness.

questions.question_text: Excimer lasers are created through the recombination of noble gases and halogens. Select the correct noble gas which is paired with fluorine to obtain excimer lasers.
questions.explanation: Excimer lasers are ultraviolet lasers formed from an excited dimer of a noble gas and a halogen. The most common example is xenon fluoride (XeF). Xenon, when combined with fluorine in an excited state, produces intense ultraviolet light used in semiconductor photolithography, LASIK eye surgery, and microfabrication. Helium and neon form other types of lasers (like He-Ne), but not excimer lasers with fluorine. Radon is radioactive and unsuitable. Hence, xenon is the correct noble gas paired with fluorine for excimer laser production.

questions.question_text: The relation of several characters of a word, or signature or line of writing to an actual or imaginary baseline, is known as:
questions.explanation: In forensic handwriting analysis, alignment describes how words, characters, or entire lines of writing relate to a baseline—whether the strokes remain steady, rise above, or dip below an actual or imaginary line. This is one of the most important features used to compare known and questioned documents. Other handwriting features like slant (angle of strokes), word spacing (gaps between words), and arrangement (overall page layout) provide additional but distinct information.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following products obtained from crude oil in increasing order of their boiling point:
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbon boiling points rise with increasing molecular weight and intermolecular forces. Propane (C3H8) has the lowest boiling point (-42 °C). Butane (C4H10) comes next (-0.5 °C). Octane (C8H18), a liquid fuel component, boils near 125 °C. Xylene (C8H10), an aromatic with greater polarizability, boils slightly higher (~138-144 °C). Kerosene, a mixture of long-chain hydrocarbons (C12-C15), has the highest boiling point, ranging 150-300 °C. Thus the correct increasing order is: Propane -> Butane -> Octane -> Xylene -> Kerosene.

questions.question_text: Elements placed in group VI of periodic table consists of transition metals known for their strength and corrosion resistance. Which of the following element from this group is commonly used to plate screwdriver shafts and blades?
questions.explanation: Chromium is a Group VI transition metal noted for exceptional hardness, high corrosion resistance, and shiny metallic finish. Because of these properties, it is commonly used to electroplate steel tools such as screwdriver shafts and blades. The plating provides durability and resistance to wear. Iron itself rusts, zinc is mainly used for galvanizing, and nickel plating is decorative but less common for screwdriver shafts compared to chromium.

questions.question_text: The shape of the ........... determines the form and the pattern of ridges on the skin surface.
questions.explanation: Fingerprint ridges originate from the dermal papillae, the upward projections of the dermis into the epidermis. These papillae determine the unique ridge flow and minutiae that appear on the skin surface. Since epidermis simply follows the contour of the papillae, fingerprints remain permanent and unique throughout life. Ridge islands, on the other hand, are just local ridge features, not the developmental source of patterns.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: X-ray absorption (A-III): Excites inner-shell electrons due to very high photon energy. UV absorption (B-II): Promotes bonding/valence electrons to higher orbitals. Microwave absorption (C-IV): Causes rotational transitions in molecules, useful for studying molecular structure. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (D-I): Involves transitions of the spin states of nuclei in a magnetic field, fundamental for NMR spectroscopy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are NOT correct?

statements.label: A
statements.text: The hand-lettering causes details of forms to assume somewhat lower importance.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Hand-lettering identification is not complete without consideration of retracing, pen dragging and retouching.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The execution of hand-lettering is not significant in the identification.

statements.label: D
statements.text: With extensive hand-lettering, such as a page or more, writers may revert to segments of cursive writing (in case of disguise writings).

questions.explanation: In hand-lettering, the form details (proportions, junctions, stroke formations) remain central to identification; disguisers often over-focus on drawing letter shapes, which actually preserves many individual traits—so (A) is not correct. Likewise, the execution (speed/fluency, pen lifts, pen pressure rhythm, line quality) is a key evidentiary domain—so (C) is not correct. A complete evaluation does consider retracing/pen dragging/retouching (B), and in extended disguised writing, reversion to natural cursive segments is common (D).

questions.question_text: Using high performance liquid chromatography, the separated analyte could be identified by using their:
questions.explanation: In HPLC, an analyte is characterized under fixed conditions by its retention time ( $t^R$ ) and the derived, column/flow-independent capacity factor ( $k' = (t^R - t^0)/t^0$ ). These two together provide robust identity evidence when combined with stationary/mobile phase and temperature. "Migration time/factor" are electrophoresis terms; dead time ( $t^0$ ) defines void volume and serves as a reference rather than a direct identifier.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:

match_right.label: II
match_right.text: It has an extractor flange that is larger in diameter than cartridge case body and a groove around the case.

match_right.label: III
match_right.text: It has an extractor flange having same diameter as of the cartridge case and a groove around the body of cartridge case.

match_right.label: IV
match_right.text: It has an extractor flange that is smaller than the diameter of case and groove around the body of the case.

questions.explanation: Rebated (A-IV): rim (extractor flange) smaller than body diameter, with groove. Rimless (B-III): rim same as body diameter, with extractor groove. Rimmed (C-I): prominent extractor flange projecting beyond body (classic revolver types). Semi-rimmed (D-II): rim slightly larger than body, with groove—intermediate between rimmed and rimless.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in a proper sequence for automatic action of the gun:
questions.explanation: After a shot, the action extracts the spent case (D) and ejects it (E). Rearward/return motion cocks the striker or hammer (B), then the bolt/slide loads a fresh round from the magazine (C). The next trigger press initiates firing (A). This cycle repeats automatically until the magazine is empty or the action is interrupted.

questions.question_text: Arrange the correct sequence for the Bedside test of ethanol:

statements.label: C
statements.text: A characteristic strong fruity odor confirms positive test for ethanol

statements.label: D
statements.text: Place 1 ml of unknown solution in a test tube

questions.explanation: For the bedside ethanol (ethyl acetate odor) test, place 1 mL sample (D) -> add 1 mL acetic acid (A) -> add 1 drop conc. H2SO4 as catalyst (E) -> gently heat ~1 min (B) -> a strong fruity odor of ethyl acetate indicates ethanol (C). The sequence mirrors acid-catalyzed esterification of ethanol with acetic acid.

questions.question_text: The age of an individual, upto 25 years, can be best determined, within a range of one to two years, from:
questions.explanation: For individuals up to about 25 years, the ossification of bones (B) and the changes of puberty (E) give the most reliable indicators of age, accurate to within 1–2 years. Ossification centers appear and fuse at well-established ages, while puberty brings predictable physiological changes. Grey hair (A) and weight (D) vary widely with genetics, nutrition, and lifestyle. Birth records (C) provide exact age but are not a biological indicator.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: Arsine (A-III): Used in metallurgy for lead plating. Copper arsenite (B-I): Known as "Scheele's Green", once used as a colouring agent for wallpapers, toys, and fabrics. Lead arsenate (C-IV): Historically used as an insecticide in orchards. Sulfides of arsenic (D-II): Compounds like realgar and orpiment were sometimes used as depilatories.

questions.question_text: Which of the undermentioned element is added to crystal glass for the purpose of making the glass sparkle?
questions.explanation: Lead oxide is added to crystal glass to increase its refractive index, which makes the glass sparkle and gives it brilliance. This is why lead crystal glassware has such characteristic brightness and resonance. Copper, silver, and aluminium are not used for this purpose.

questions.question_text: Hypostasis helps to determine which of the following?
questions.explanation: Hypostasis (postmortem lividity or livor mortis) refers to the settling of blood in dependent parts of the body after death. Its onset, distribution, and fixation provide an estimate of the time since death. It does not directly indicate mode of death, type, or sequence of injuries.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:

match_right.label: I
match_right.text: Is the proportion of alleles, at a given locus

match_right.label: II
match_right.text: Ability of a genetic marker to distinguish between different individuals in a population

match_right.label: III
match_right.text: It allows predictions of genotype frequencies based on allelic frequencies

match_right.label: IV
match_right.text: Can be calculated directly by counting the number of alleles of one type at a given locus and dividing it by the total number of alleles at that locus in a sampled population

questions.explanation: Hardy-Weinberg Principle (A-III): Predicts genotype frequencies from allele frequencies in a population. Heterozygosity (B-I): Refers to the proportion of alleles that are different at a given locus in individuals. Allele frequency (C-IV): Calculated as the number of alleles of one type divided by the total alleles in the population sample. Power of discrimination (D-II): Measures how well a genetic marker distinguishes between individuals.

questions.question_text: Acid phosphatase has optimal activity in acidic pH environment. The forensic importance of acid phosphatase is:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is present in seminal fluid.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Acid phosphatase isoenzymes are found in other tissues also.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Acid phosphatase activity cannot be detected from dry seminal stains stored at -20°C upto 1 year.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Acid phosphatase level in semen are not affected by vasectomies.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Radio immunoassay is not a sensitive test for identification of acid phosphatase.

questions.explanation: The forensic value of acid phosphatase lies in its strong presence in seminal fluid and its use as a presumptive marker in sexual assault investigations. Semen contains several prostate-derived markers like PSA (A). Acid phosphatase is also found in other tissues like liver and spleen (B), and its levels are not affected by vasectomies (D). Statements C and E are false.

questions.question_text: The pattern of unidentified tyre marks is assigned a set of codes for pattern features, such as waves, lines, diamonds, zigzags, curves, blocks etc. which then forms the basis of the database search, is known as:
questions.explanation: Tread Mate is the correct database system for tyre tread evidence. Investigators examine tyre marks at a crime scene, assign codes to tread features (such as zigzags, waves, diamonds, or blocks), and then enter these codes into the database. The system compares these features against known manufacturer specifications, helping forensic experts identify the make, model, and sometimes the tire. This is vital in linking a suspect vehicle to a crime scene.

questions.question_text: The finger marks, caused by the contact of finger with a malleable substance that subsequently retains a three-dimensional image of the print, are known as:
questions.explanation: When a finger presses against a soft, pliable material such as wax, soap, putty, or clay, it leaves a three-dimensional impression of the ridge pattern. These are known as indented visible marks or plastic prints. Unlike latent prints (invisible residues requiring chemical or physical development), indented marks are visible to the naked eye and retain ridge depth. Positive or negative visible marks, by contrast, are two-dimensional prints caused by residues like sweat, dust, or blood.

questions.question_text: Certain differences exist between the skull of individuals belonging to different races, which can be determined by all these except:
questions.explanation: Skull analysis for ancestry determination relies on cranial indices that measure proportions of the skull: Height Index (HI), Cephalic Index (CI), and Nasal Index (NI). The Lens Age Index (LAI), however, measures biochemical changes in the crystalline lens of the eye to estimate age at death and has no role in ancestry determination.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: Each of these chemicals has a specific role in paper manufacture: Starches (A-III) improve strength, stiffness, and surface bonding. Kaolin (B-II) is a fine clay used as a filler and coating pigment to increase opacity. Alum (C-IV) controls pH and is used in sizing to bind rosin to fibres. Waxes (D-I) provide water resistance and smooth surface finish.

questions.question_text: Which of these is used as a chemical enhancement reagent for detecting blood stains?
questions.explanation: Leuco Crystal Violet (LCV) is widely used in forensic science as a chemical enhancement reagent for visualizing bloodstains. It is initially colorless but, in the presence of hemoglobin and hydrogen peroxide, gets oxidized to crystal violet—a bright purple dye. This reaction highlights latent or faint bloodstains, even on surfaces where blood might have been cleaned or diluted, making it a valuable presumptive test in crime scene investigations.

questions.question_text: Name the test where a mould is filled with cement paste, submerged in water and boiled to measure the expansion:
questions.explanation: The Le Chatelier test determines the soundness of cement, i.e., its ability to retain volume stability after setting. A mould filled with cement paste is submerged in water and then boiled. Expansion is measured to detect unsoundness caused by free lime or magnesia. Although autoclave methods also test soundness, the description given (boiling water bath method) specifically matches the Le Chatelier test.

questions.question_text: The ............ of the lens is a set of blades that forms the variable lens openings.
questions.explanation: The diaphragm in a lens is a system of overlapping blades that form a variable opening. This regulates how much light enters the camera. The opening itself is called the aperture, which is measured in f-stops. The diaphragm works much like the iris of the eye—expanding or contracting to control light. Aberrations are lens defects, while exposure meters measure light levels but are not part of the lens itself.

questions.question_text: What are "immobilines" in the context of isoelectric focusing?

options.option_text: Buffer that fixes the pH after focusing
Modified acrylamide monomers with acidic or basic properties

questions.explanation: In isoelectric focusing, immobilines are modified acrylamide monomers carrying acidic or basic functional groups. When incorporated into the gel, they establish a fixed pH gradient. This eliminates drift associated with carrier ampholytes and allows proteins to migrate until they reach their isoelectric point (pI). Because immobilines "immobilize" the pH, they provide reproducibility and sharper separation in protein analysis.

questions.question_text: A percussion cup having 'V' shaped anvil, is known as:
questions.explanation: The Boxer primer contains a self-contained V-shaped anvil inside the primer cup. When struck by the firing pin, the priming compound is crushed between the cup and the anvil, igniting the propellant. Boxer primers are easy to reload because the cartridge has a single central flash hole. By contrast, Berdan primers have two flash holes and the anvil built into the cartridge case, making reloading more difficult.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:

match_left.label: A
match_left.text: The firearms made by blacksmith by not adhering to any specification.

match_left.label: B
match_left.text: In the priming mixture potassium chlorate acts as

match_left.label: C
match_left.text: Small-pocket firearms having multiple barrels, each of which is loaded and fired separately.

match_left.label: D
match_left.text: Material used for coating propellant grains to eliminate static electricity.

questions.explanation: Zip-guns (A-IV) are crude firearms manufactured by local blacksmiths. Potassium chlorate (B-III) acts as an oxidizer in priming mixtures. Derringers (C-I) are small-pocket firearms with multiple barrels. Graphite (D-II) is used to coat propellant grains, reducing static electricity and improving flow.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in chronological order regarding the establishment of CFSL's in India.
questions.explanation: The chronological order of CFSL establishments in India is: Calcutta (Kolkata) - the first CFSL, established in 1957. Hyderabad - the second, in 1967. Delhi - set up later in 1968. Pune - established much later in 1977.

questions.question_text: Insects can be used to determine many factors about a death scene, except:

options.option_text: Whether the body has been moved after death
The nature of poison consumed cannot be determined

questions.explanation: Forensic entomology uses insect evidence to estimate the time since death, determine if the body was moved, and sometimes indicate wound location based on insect colonization patterns. However, while some toxins may affect insect development, insect evidence generally cannot reliably identify the specific poison consumed by the deceased.

questions.question_text: The ballistic co-efficient of the projectile (C) is given by:

options.option_text: (2gR)^0.5 [where g = gravitation acceleration, R = earth's radius]
W / nd^2 [where W = weight of the projectile, d = cross-sectional diameter and n = coefficient of reduction]
(AV^n) [where 'A' and 'n' = constants, V = velocity of the projectile]
W / nd^2 [where W = weight of the projectile, d = cross-sectional diameter]

questions.explanation: The ballistic coefficient (C) measures how well a projectile overcomes air resistance. It is expressed as:  $C = W / nd^2$  where W is the weight of the projectile, d its cross-sectional diameter, and n a coefficient of form or reduction. This formula balances mass and drag surface area, making it fundamental in external ballistics.

questions.question_text: The fingerprint pattern of a person is as follows: Whorl pattern on right middle, right little, left index, left middle fingers; arch pattern present on right ring and left thumb and rest all the fingers have loop pattern. Based on the above pattern, what will be the primary classification?
questions.explanation: In Henry's Primary Classification, values are assigned to whorl patterns in a specific finger order. Whorls are present on: Right middle (value 2), Right little (value 16), Left index (value 8), Left middle (value 4). Total for even fingers =  $16 + 4 = 20$  -> add  $1 = 21$ . Total for odd fingers =  $2 + 8 = 10$  -> add  $1 = 11$ . Thus, the fraction reduces to 5/13 when normalized in the system's ratio form.

questions.question_text: Metabolism of alcohol is accomplished through which of the undermentioned pathway in the liver?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is metabolized in the liver primarily through three pathways: Alcohol dehydrogenase pathway (B) is the main enzymatic route. Microsomal ethanol oxidizing system (D) involves cytochrome P450 2E1, active at higher concentrations of ethanol. Peroxidase catalase system (E) is a minor pathway using catalase and hydrogen peroxide. Cholinergic (A) and Cytochrome P-450 as a standalone (C) are not correct.

questions.question_text: The primary element used for making of a firearm cartridge case belongs to which block of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Firearm cartridge cases are mainly made of brass, an alloy of copper and zinc. Both copper (atomic number 29) and zinc (atomic number 30) belong to the d-block (transition metals) of the periodic table. These metals provide the strength, malleability, and resistance to corrosion required for cartridge cases.

questions.question_text: The phenomenon, in which the darker of two crossing lines appears to be upper most, even if it was written first, is called:
questions.explanation: When two ink lines cross, the darker line often appears to be on top, regardless of which was written first. This is a classic optical illusion in questioned document examination. It can mislead the examiner, and special techniques (like microscopy or electrostatic methods) are used to determine the actual sequence of strokes.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in proper sequence regarding the filing arrangement of the fingerprint record slips by National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB):
questions.explanation: The filing system of fingerprint record slips used by the NCRB follows the principles of Henry's Classification System: Primary classification (A) -> Secondary classification (C) -> Major classification (B) -> Sub-secondary classification (E) -> Final classification (D).

questions.question_text: The act of inserting writing or typewriting between two lines of writing, is known as:
questions.explanation: In forensic document analysis, interlineation refers to inserting new writing or typing between two existing lines of text. It is a common alteration technique in fraudulent documents. Addition is general insertion, restoration means bringing back erased writing, and decipherment refers to reading obscured or hidden writing.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following in a proper sequence in determining the range of fire from near to farthest:
questions.explanation: To determine the range of fire, forensic experts carefully study physical marks left on the target. From nearest to farthest, the effects are: Muzzle pattern (Contact shot) (B) -> Scorching (C) -> Blackening (E) -> Tattooing (D) -> Metallic residue (A). Thus, the correct sequence is B, C, E, D, A.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:

match_right.label: I
match_right.text: Biologically active compound that is biotransformed in-vivo in a rapid and predictable manner into nontoxic moieties.

match_right.label: II
match_right.text: Biologically active compound with a high lipid solubility or high water solubility having a long biological half life.

match_right.label: III
match_right.text: Usually, two synergistic drugs which are attached to each other.

match_right.label: IV
match_right.text: Compound that contains an active drug linked to a certain group that can be removed enzymatically.

questions.explanation: Hard prodrug (A-II): A biologically active compound designed with high stability and long half-life, often highly lipid- or water-soluble, that remains in the body for prolonged periods. Soft prodrug (B-I): A biologically active compound deliberately designed to be rapidly and predictably broken down into inactive, non-toxic metabolites, minimizing accumulation and toxicity. Carrier-linked prodrug (C-IV): Consists of an active drug molecule attached to a carrier group that is cleaved enzymatically to release the active drug. Mutual prodrug (D-III): Two synergistic drugs linked together chemically, so that both contribute to therapeutic action after cleavage.

questions.question_text: The formation of a blood droplet is a complex event, which is influenced by below mentioned properties, except:
questions.explanation: Blood droplet formation is governed by physical properties and forces: Viscosity (internal resistance to flow), Surface tension (causes spherical shape), and Gravity (pulls the droplet downward). Adhesive force relates to attraction between blood and a surface but is not a direct factor in the initial formation of a free-falling droplet.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: The number of pellets per ounce (28.35 g) is standardized for different shotgun shot sizes: A-shot (A-III): ~50 pellets. SG-shot (B-II): ~8 pellets. B-shot (C-IV): ~80 pellets. SSG-shot (D-I): ~15 pellets.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:

match_right.label: I
match_right.text: constitutes the backbone of an identification

match_right.label: II
match_right.text: are used by the document examiners as the basis for identification or non-identification of questioned document

match_right.label: III
match_right.text: is an integral part of natural writing

match_right.label: IV
match_right.text: may result from family association, trade training, education and writing system studied

questions.explanation: Class characteristics (A-IV): Common features resulting from similar training, education, or writing systems. Individual characteristics (B-I): Unique, personal handwriting traits that serve as the backbone of identification. Writing standards (C-II): Authentic, known handwriting samples used as the basis of comparison. Writing variation (D-III): Natural differences that occur when the same writer produces multiple writings.

questions.question_text: 0.303 inch rifle, which was most commonly used in the police forces in India, had which of the following action:
questions.explanation: The .303 British Lee-Enfield—issued widely to Indian police and military—uses a manual bolt. The shooter lifts and pulls the bolt to extract/eject the spent case, then pushes it forward to chamber the next round. This action is prized for reliability, strength, and good accuracy.

questions.question_text: Arrange in sequence, the putrefaction of internal organs in reverse action:
questions.explanation: Standard forward order of internal organ putrefaction (earliest -> latest) is generally: B (larynx/trachea) -> C (stomach & intestine) -> D (spleen) -> E (liver) -> A (brain). The question asks for the reverse order (latest -> earliest), which should therefore be: A -> E -> D -> C -> B. None of the four choices match A, E, D, C, B, so the correct response is that no option provided is accurate.

questions.question_text: What is meant by 'over-text' while referring to secret writing?
questions.explanation: In secret writing, over-text is the ordinary, visible text written on the page to mask the presence of hidden/invisible "under-text". It's camouflage for clandestine messages (e.g., invisible ink) so the document appears innocuous.

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: ABO grouping -> III (Agglutination): ABO types are identified by agglutination with specific antisera. Blood proteins -> I (Electrophoresis): Serum/plasma proteins are separated by migration methods. Gm & Inv system -> IV (Antibody neutralization): Immunoglobulin allotypes are typed via neutralization methods. Blood stain -> II (Benzidine test): A classic presumptive test exploiting hemoglobin's peroxidase-like activity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a red cell enzyme?
questions.explanation: Of the choices, the only category that correctly maps to enzymes present in red cells is protease (RBCs contain proteolytic activities such as calpain/proteasomal components). Sucrase is a brush-border intestinal enzyme, amylase is chiefly salivary/pancreatic (forensic marker for saliva, not RBC), and haptoglobin is a plasma glycoprotein (hemoglobin-binding), not an enzyme.

questions.question_text: After death of humans, tissues and cells survive for a varying period depending upon their oxygen requirement, and when these individual tissues and cells die, it is termed as:
questions.explanation: Somatic death is the complete and irreversible cessation of life functions of the organism as a whole. After somatic death, individual tissues and cells continue to survive for a variable time depending on their oxygen demand. When they eventually die, this process is called molecular death. Hence, the correct term for tissue/cell-level death after somatic death is molecular death.

questions.question_text: The amount of degree of yaw depends upon which of the following:

statements.label: B
statements.text: Rate of the twist of the barrel

statements.label: D
statements.text: Diameter and cross-sectional density of the bullet

questions.explanation: The yaw of a bullet is its deviation from its straight axis during flight. The amount or degree of yaw depends on: Rate of twist of the barrel (B), Density of the air (C), and Diameter and cross-sectional density of the bullet (D). It is not significantly dependent on cartridge case length (A) or barrel length (E).

questions.question_text: Match List-I with List-II:
questions.explanation: Scratches -> IV (Abrasions): Superficial damage to skin surface. Contusions -> III (Bruises): Discoloration caused by blood leakage under the skin due to blunt trauma. Split -> I (Laceration): Tearing of tissue due to blunt force. Cuts -> II (Incised wound): Clean wounds caused by sharp-edged instruments.

questions.question_text: ABH group specific substances are found in which of these:
questions.explanation: Secretors: About 80% of people are secretors, meaning they secrete ABH blood group-specific substances into body fluids such as saliva, semen, vaginal fluid, sweat. Hair root of secretor (A) and semen of secretor (C) contain ABH substances. Non-secretors do not secrete ABH substances into body fluids, so (B) saliva of non-secretor and (D) vaginal secretion of non-secretor will not contain them.

questions.question_text: Which part of the Constitution of India deals with Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Constitution of India. They guarantee civil liberties such as equality, freedom, rights against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies.

questions.question_text: Methamphetamine is generally best classified under which group of drugs?
questions.explanation: Methamphetamine belongs to the stimulant group of drugs. It increases central nervous system activity, flooding the brain with dopamine, leading to euphoria, hyperactivity, and wakefulness. Unlike depressants or deliriants, it excites neural functions, which explains its misuse to keep soldiers awake during wartime.

questions.question_text: What is the IUPAC name of methamphetamine mentioned in the above story?
questions.explanation: The IUPAC name of methamphetamine is N-methyl-1-phenylpropan-2-amine. It is a substituted phenethylamine and amphetamine derivative, with a methyl group on the nitrogen atom and a phenyl group attached to the first carbon of a propane chain.

questions.question_text: After administration of methamphetamine, it is metabolized and excreted from the body in the form of metabolite. Name the primary metabolite of methamphetamine:
questions.explanation: The primary metabolite of methamphetamine is pholedrine. The drug undergoes hepatic metabolism mainly through hydroxylation and N-demethylation, producing active metabolites that may also contribute to stimulant effects before excretion.

questions.question_text: Based on the above story, what are the common symptoms experienced by the users of the drug?

options.option_text: Extreme sleepiness, low heart rate, relaxed muscle
Loss of hearing, cold sweats, joint inflammation

questions.explanation: Methamphetamine causes intense release of dopamine, resulting in extreme euphoria. Chronic use produces paranoia, hallucinations, neurological and brain damage. This matches the passage's mention of "extreme euphoria", "severe addiction", "paranoia", and "neurological damage".

questions.question_text: Which part of the ephedra plant is used to extract the alkaloid?
questions.explanation: The main alkaloid ephedrine is obtained from the stem of the Ephedra plant (a desert shrub). This plant has been traditionally used in Chinese medicine as a decongestant and stimulant. The stem is the part richest in alkaloid content.

questions.question_text: Semi-automatic pistols can be operated by which of the following actions?
questions.explanation: Semi-automatic pistols operate through a recoiling slide action. After firing, the slide moves backward, ejecting the spent cartridge case, and then moves forward, chambering a new round. This allows rapid successive firing with each trigger pull. Lever action and hinge action are typical of rifles or shotguns, while "double action" refers to a trigger mechanism, not the operating cycle.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statement is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: The semi-automatic throw cartridge cases in a definite direction to a certain distance.
From the position of the fired shell, it is possible to find the position of the culprit at the time of firing.
The position of the projectile does not help in the reconstruction of the occurrence.
X-rays help to locate the position of the projectiles inside the body.

questions.explanation: This is the incorrect statement. In fact, the projectile's position, trajectory, and recovery location are crucial in reconstructing how the incident occurred (shooter's position, range, and angle). Other statements are correct: semi-automatics eject cases in a predictable direction, fired shell position helps approximate shooter location, and X-rays are standard in locating projectiles within the body.

questions.question_text: Post-mortem examination in firearm cases helps to determine the following, except:

options.option_text: Does not ascertain the nature of the firearm used

questions.explanation: A post-mortem in firearm cases can determine: Cause of death (e.g., hemorrhage due to bullet injury), Nature of death (homicidal, suicidal, accidental), and Direction of fire (entry/exit wound study). However, it cannot by itself identify the specific firearm type (revolver, pistol, rifle). That requires ballistic examination.

questions.question_text: The visit of IO to the scene of crime, if not logged could be best verified by which of these?
questions.explanation: If the Investigating Officer's (IO) visit to the scene was not properly logged, the best independent verification comes from CCTV footage covering the location. Witness testimony, footprints, or sniffer dogs may support investigation, but CCTV provides objective and time-stamped confirmation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT correct for powder tattooing phenomenon?

options.option_text: They appeared as reddish brown to orange-red coloration

questions.explanation: Powder tattooing (stippling) is caused by unburnt or partially burnt powder particles striking and embedding in the skin, producing punctate reddish-brown/orange abrasions. It is an ante-mortem phenomenon (needs circulation for inflammatory reaction), and appears as punctate abrasions with reddish-brown coloration. But it is not the same as powder burns. Powder burns result from flame and hot gases, whereas tattooing is due to impact of solid particles.
